candidates.reason: A map-style combinator can group corresponding positions from multiple sequences and stop when the shortest input ends.
candidates.application_scope: A pairing helper for an existing loop; the source establishes ordered callbacks and shortest-input termination.

candidates.application_scope: Loop syntax and shared termination; ordinary list or vector clauses stop the loop when one reaches its endpoint.

Baseline B — C07
Decision cutoff: 2000-08-03. Translation by GPT-6 Astra Pro in an internal separate context.

Four candidates were verified through primary pages after their items appeared in opened awesome catalogues. Three have dated pre-cutoff evidence; the fourth remains undated live evidence.

1. Common Lisp sequence map
Verification: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/Groups/AI/html/cltl/clm/node143.html
Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/GustavBertram/awesome-common-lisp-learning
This map combines the same position across multiple inputs and terminates at the shortest. A grouping callback supplies a model for a pairing helper consumed by an existing loop. Its ordered calls are also relevant. Python's custom sequence access and end-exception behavior would still require a separately specified adapter.
Date: pre-decision; the archive identifies the book as the 1990 second edition.

2. Common Lisp LOOP with multiple iteration clauses
Verification: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs.cmu.edu/project/ai-repository/ai/html/cltl/clm/node244.html
Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/GustavBertram/awesome-common-lisp-learning
Several sequence bindings can feed one loop body, with an endpoint terminating that loop. This supplies an alternative syntax model for corresponding-element traversal. Transfer entails additional syntax and a clear distinction between sequential and parallel stepping; compatibility with Python custom sequences is not established.
Date: pre-decision; the book is dated 1990 and the opened chapter reports adoption in January 1989.

3. R5RS Scheme map and for-each
Verification: https://groups.csail.mit.edu/mac/ftpdir/scheme-reports/r5rs-html/r5rs_8.html
Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/theodesp/awesome-scheme
The multi-list interface pairs corresponding elements under an equal-length precondition. For-each additionally guarantees ordered calls for side effects. This is useful when defining an explicit input contract, but it does not establish automatic rejection of unequal inputs and applies to lists rather than Python's custom sequence protocol.
Date: pre-decision; the opened report's HTML edition is dated 19 May 1999.

4. more-itertools zip_offset
Verification: https://more-itertools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html
Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/vinta/awesome-python
Zero offsets yield positional pairing; shortest-input termination is the default, while longest=True explicitly enables filling. This illustrates making padding a visible choice. The library builds on modern Python zip, so it is not independent historical evidence for the design under study.
Date: unknown. The opened live documentation identifies version 11.2.1 and its history places this function in 2.5.0, but no release timestamp was verified; the tags page was blocked.

The Python adaptations above are model translations, not claims of implementation, deployment, or demonstrated usefulness. An adapter would still need to preserve the supplied problem's index-based user-defined sequence contract and distinguish normal exhaustion from other errors.
